struck: Homes in The Preserve at Pine Lakes and Pine Lakes Estates resold for $70,000 to $1,140,000.
use: About 17 resales in The Preserve and Pine Lakes Estates sold mostly between $540,000 and $670,000.

struck: 54 homes were sold in Grande Dunes by companies that sold 4 or more there, mostly home builders.

struck: The Farm at Carolina Forest: the county maps 273 parcels under this name; 262 are homes.
use: The Farm at Carolina Forest is 1,571 homes.

struck: Homes in The Farm at Carolina Forest resold for $140,000 to $463,000. The middle sale was $368,500.
use: Use $325,000 for all homes or $352,000 for detached houses.

pattern: \bat least part of it has an HOA
struck: County records show owners' associations holding common land in The Farm at Carolina Forest, so at least part of it has an HOA.
use: (Use the HOA budget rows: the HOA collects assessments on every home.)

struck: From the reference point, the closest large grocery store by car, Lowes Foods, is about 6 minutes, 1.8 miles.

use: Grand Strand Medical Center, a 403-bed hospital at 809 82nd Parkway, is about 13 minutes and 6 miles by car from the middle of The Farm.

struck: Its emergency department has been open since 2019.
use: Its emergency department there is open 24 hours a day.

struck: In the county's copy of the FEMA flood map, 271 of the 271 address points in The Farm at Carolina Forest sit outside the high-risk flood zones.

struck: The nearest public beach access by car is about 15 minutes, 7.0 miles.
use: The nearest public beach access by car is about 15 minutes, 6.5 miles.

struck: Homes in Barefoot Resort resold for $338,000 to $591,500. The middle sale was $430,000.
use: Resales in these Barefoot sections, mostly condos, sold at a middle of about $430,000.

struck: So a buyer's tax is figured on about what the home is worth, close to the price paid.

struck: The middle policy cost $1,463 a year with FEMA's fees and surcharges.
use: It cost a middle $1,258 a year when it covered the owner's main home, and $1,463 across all single-family policies, including second homes.

struck: The city's bond for that work is scheduled to be paid off in April 2028.

struck: A beach cabana on the ocean at 4611 South Ocean Boulevard for owners in its association, reached by a beach shuttle.
use: A shuttle runs from the neighborhoods to the public beach access at 46th Street on weekends in April and May and daily from June 1 to September 6.

struck: The North Tower pool is on the parcel PARCEL IX owned by the Barefoot Resort Residential Owners Association.
use: The North Tower pool and the Residents' Club pool are on parcels listed to the Barefoot Resort Residential Association.

struck: The Two Mile Waterway Trail is open to everyone.
use: The Two Mile Waterway Trail is open to the public from sunrise to sunset.

pattern: \bamenity center has pools and a clubhouse|\bclubhouse pool

struck: Pools and clubhouse.
use: Pool and buildings.

pattern: \bon a point in the lake, with[^.]{0,40}\btennis courts

struck: The association's pool complex sits beside a lake, with tennis courts and a playground next to it.
use: The association's pool complex is beside a lake, with a tennis court, a basketball court and a play area next to it.

struck: Rosewood Landing, a county boat ramp on the Intracoastal Waterway, is a short drive away.
use: Rosewood Landing, a county boat ramp on the Intracoastal Waterway, is about 2 miles away in a straight line, and about 5 miles by road.

struck: 11. Forestbrook Estates: a low HOA fee near the Waterway
use: 11. Forestbrook Estates: a low HOA fee about 2 miles from the Waterway

use: The association's amenity area, beside a lake, has a pool complex, a building, courts for tennis or pickleball, a basketball court and a playground.

pattern: \bown pool and clubhouse|\bbike trail passes close by

struck: Grand Park, with picnic shelters, ball fields and a playground, is next to the homes, and Myrtle Beach State Park is about a mile away.
use: Grand Park, with picnic shelters, ball fields and a playground, is about 0.1 mile from the nearest homes, and Myrtle Beach State Park is about a mile away.

struck: Fuller Park in Surfside Beach, with tennis courts and a playground, and the Surfside Beach pier are both under 2 miles away.
use: Fuller Park in Surfside Beach, with a playground, and the Surfside Beach Fishing Pier are both under 2 miles away.

struck: A public beach access with a pay lot and the Surfside Beach Fishing Pier are both a short walk away.
use: The Surfside Beach Fishing Pier is about 0.3 mile away.

struck: A normal day can be a walk to the pier in the morning and an evening on the beach.
use: A normal day can be a trip to the pier in the morning and an evening on the beach.

struck: Its older streets are wooded, and the association owns the lakes and canals that run between the homes.
use: Its older streets are wooded, and the association owns lake and canal land among the homes.

struck: Burgess Park, with a playground and a basketball court, is a short drive away.
use: Burgess Park, with a playground and a basketball court, is about 2.5 miles away in a straight line.

struck: Most homes for sale here are condos, built in the 2000s or since 2020, with about 2,500 square feet.
use: Of the 8 condos for sale, 3 were built in 2002 and have about 1,800 square feet, and 5 were built since 2022 and have 2,400 to 2,800 square feet.

struck: Most houses for sale here are new, built since 2023, with about 3,100 square feet.
use: Most houses for sale here were built since 2023 and have about 3,100 square feet.

struck: Most houses for sale here were built in the 2010s and have about 2,400 square feet.
use: Most houses for sale here were built in the 2000s and 2010s and have about 2,400 square feet.

pattern: \bMost houses for sale here were built in the 1970s
struck: Most houses for sale here were built in the 1970s and 1980s and have about 2,000 square feet.
use: Of the 6 houses for sale, 5 were built in the 1970s and 1980s and the middle one has about 2,000 square feet.

struck: Most houses for sale here were built around 2010 and have about 2,400 square feet.
use: The 6 houses for sale were built from 2007 to 2015, and the middle one has about 2,400 square feet.

struck: Ken Tomlinson designed its golf course, Tidewater Golf Club, a par-72 public course.
use: Tidewater Golf Club, a par-72 public course credited to Ken Tomlinson, has its fairways between the streets.

pattern: \brebuilt after Hurricane Hugo|\bholds the U\.?S\.? record
struck: Cherry Grove Pier, built in the 1950s and rebuilt after Hurricane Hugo, holds the U.S. record for the largest tiger shark landed from shore.
use: Cherry Grove Pier was built in the 1950s, and in 1964 a 1,780-pound tiger shark was landed from it, a world record at the time.

pattern: National Golf Course of the Year
struck: It was named National Golf Course of the Year in 2009.
use: It was named course of the year by the National Golf Course Owners Association in 2009.

pattern: Sports Illustrated was born|\bholds the Myrtle Beach Golf Hall of Fame
struck: Its clubhouse is on the National Register of Historic Places, Sports Illustrated was born there, and it holds the Myrtle Beach Golf Hall of Fame.
use: Its clubhouse is on the National Register of Historic Places, and Time-Life executives planned Sports Illustrated there in 1954.

pattern: \bland under Surfside Beach was a rice plantation
struck: The land under Surfside Beach was a rice plantation called The Ark.
use: Surfside Beach began as part of a rice plantation called The Ark.

struck: On streets with sailing names: Spinnaker Drive, Topsail Lane, Brigantine Road.
use: Some of its streets have sailing names: Spinnaker Drive, Topsail Lane, Brigantine Road.

struck: Its streets are named for wildflowers and woodland plants, such as Lady Slipper Drive, Fiddlehead Way and Yellow Morel Way, off Rachel Carson Parkway.
use: Many of its streets are named for plants, such as Lady Slipper Drive, Fiddlehead Way and Dewberry Lane.

struck: Whose street names follow the deer: Deer Creek Road, Doe Drive, Deer Park Lane.
use: With street names from wildlife, such as Deer Creek Road, Doe Drive and Loon Court.

pattern: \btakes its street names from the woods
struck: It takes its street names from the woods: Duck Blind Place, White Tail Place, Hunters Road, Little Fawn Way.
use: It takes many of its street names from the woods and hunting: Duck Blind Place, White Tail Place, Hunters Road, Little Fawn Way.

pattern: \bThe streets nearby are named for ducks|\bBlue Wing Drive
struck: The streets nearby are named for ducks: Blue Wing Drive, Green Wing Drive, Teal Drive, Eider Drive.
use: Some streets nearby are named for ducks: Teal Drive, Eider Drive and Shoveler Lane.

pattern: \bStreet names keep the history|\bThe streets carry seashell names|\bThe streets are named for water birds
struck: Street names keep the history. The streets carry seashell names. The streets are named for water birds.
use: Some street names recall it. Many streets carry seashell names. Many streets are named for water birds.

struck: Its houses for sale are the largest on this page, and they cost more than in any other inland neighborhood here.
use: Its houses for sale are the largest on this page, and they cost more than in the other Carolina Forest neighborhoods here.

struck: Waterbridge was started by South Carolina Coastal Development, which sold its lakes and common areas to the homeowners association in 2010.
use: Waterbridge was started by South Carolina Coastal Development, which sold open space and common areas to the homeowners association in 2010. The association looks after the lakes.

pattern: \bcanoes?\b|\btrails follow the water|\bsand volleyball|\bNext to them are a fitness center
struck: Owners can take a canoe out on the lakes from the community's docks, and walking trails follow the water. Next to them are a fitness center open around the clock and courts for tennis, pickleball, basketball and sand volleyball.
use: Owners can launch a kayak or other non-motorized boat on the lakes from a boat launch with a floating dock, and walking paths cross the water on bridges. The clubhouse has a fitness center open around the clock.

struck: Plantation Lakes is built along one continuous lake off Carolina Bays Parkway.
use: Plantation Lakes is built around a large lake, with about 15 miles of shoreline, off Carolina Bays Parkway.

struck: The owners' association has held about 180 acres of common areas since 2007.
use: The owners' association holds about 185 acres of common areas, deeded to it in 2007 and 2008.

struck: On a lakefront lot, the water is behind the house, and an owner can reach the amenity area by boat.
use: Many homes back onto the lake, and the amenity area has a dock.

struck: The expansion added a second amenity area with a lazy river, another pool and pickleball courts.
use: The expansion added a second amenity area with a pool and courts for tennis or pickleball.

struck: Owners may drive golf carts in the neighborhood. Owners drive golf carts on its streets.
use: Listings say golf carts are allowed, and we check the HOA rules before you offer.

struck: Lennar built Forestbrook Estates, starting in 2018.
use: Lennar developed Forestbrook Estates, starting in 2018.

pattern: \bbeside the pool is a community garden
struck: Beside the pool is a community garden, where owners can keep their own plot.
use: On the same grounds as the pool is a community garden with garden plots.

pattern: \b43-acre park beside|\b43 acres of shared land
struck: 15. Prince Creek: homes and a 43-acre park beside a Tom Fazio course in Murrells Inlet
use: 15. Prince Creek: homes beside a Tom Fazio course in Murrells Inlet

pattern: \bIt has two pools, tennis and pickleball courts, basketball
struck: It has two pools, tennis and pickleball courts, basketball, a playground and a covered pavilion with grills.
use: Its amenity area has two pools and courts for tennis and pickleball, and listings add basketball, a playground and a covered pavilion.

struck: The Hollidays built a pavilion, a general store and a few rental cottages for summer visitors, and later a fishing pier.
use: The Hollidays built a pavilion, a general store and a few rental cottages for summer visitors. A fishing pier was built later.

struck: From the middle of the neighborhood, a public beach access is a block or two away, the closest beach walk of the fifteen.
use: From a home near the middle of the neighborhood, a public beach access is about 0.1 mile away, the closest of the fifteen.

struck: Tidewater Plantation is between the Intracoastal Waterway and Cherry Grove Inlet, behind a gatehouse on Little River Neck Road.
use: Tidewater Plantation is between the Intracoastal Waterway and Cherry Grove Inlet, behind a guard house that visitors reach from Little River Neck Road.

struck: A condo or villa here pays about $780 to $800 a month in HOA fees.
use: Two-bedroom condos in the Clubhouse Villas list at about $780 to $800 a month in HOA fees, and other units in the same buildings list higher and lower.

struck: Builders are still selling new houses in its newest sections, so some streets still have building work.
use: About 90 new houses were sold here in the past year, mostly by builders, and some of its newest streets are still filling in.

struck: Its nearest beach access has no parking, so owners drive on to one that does.
use: The beach access nearest by car has no parking; the next one, with a pay lot, is about the same distance away.

struck: Pulte Homes later added land from two neighboring developments, and the county now counts about 870 homes in Berkshire Forest.
use: County records show more than 1,100 homes in Berkshire Forest and its Berkshire Village section together, and more in the older named sections.

struck: River Oaks Elementary School is at the edge of the neighborhood, on Augusta Plantation Drive.
use: River Oaks Elementary School is on Augusta Plantation Drive, next to the Berkshire Village section.

pattern: \bplanned under the name Kingsland|\blake you can take a boat on
struck: Forestbrook Estates was planned under the name Kingsland. The neighborhood has ponds but no lake you can take a boat on.
use: Forestbrook Estates was formerly known as Kingsland. The neighborhood has ponds, not a lake.

pattern: \bgrew up around the Deer Track|\btwo investors|\bcourts found the land|\bpark right at the beach
struck: The Deerfield Plantation area grew up around the Deer Track golf resort near Surfside Beach. In 2006 two investors bought the golf course land. The courts found the land carried no such restriction. So an owner with a golf cart can park right at the beach.
use: The Deerfield Plantation area is built around the old Deer Track golf courses near Surfside Beach. In 2006 two buyers bought the golf course. A special referee found no such restriction on the land, and the state Court of Appeals affirmed in 2012. The closest beach access has three parking spaces, for golf carts only.

struck: A recent renovation, led by Brauer himself, rebuilt its greens and bunkers.
use: A recent renovation, led by Brauer himself, gave it new greens and refreshed bunkers.

struck: A short walk, about 0.4 mile
use: About 0.4 mile, a 9-minute walk

struck: Lennar built every house the county approved here, around ponds, with townhomes beside them.
use: Lennar built nearly every home here, around ponds, with townhomes beside the houses.

struck: That bridge dates from 1934 and was moved here from Edenton, North Carolina, the year the courses opened.
use: That bridge dates from the 1930s and was moved here from Edenton, North Carolina, the year the courses opened.

pattern: \bdeveloper restored it and gave it to the city
struck: The resort's developer restored it and gave it to the city of North Myrtle Beach.
use: (Cut it: one source only, the resort's own history page, and that page contradicts itself on the bridge.)

pattern: \bthe lowest HOA fee for a house
struck: Of the four Carolina Forest neighborhoods here, The Farm has the lowest house prices and the lowest HOA fee for a house.
use: Of the four Carolina Forest neighborhoods here, The Farm has the lowest house prices, and its HOA fee is lower than the usual fee in the other three.

pattern: \bonly Grande Dunes has houses that sell for more
struck: Of the fifteen, only Grande Dunes has houses that sell for more.
use: Of the four Carolina Forest neighborhoods here, Plantation Lakes has the highest house prices.

pattern: townhome here pays[^.]{0,80}much more than a house

use: A townhome here pays about $300 to $680 a month in HOA fees.

pattern: \bGrande Dunes is still being built, and most houses
struck: Grande Dunes is still being built, and most houses for sale are new or not yet finished.
use: Across Grande Dunes, most houses for sale are new or not yet finished.

struck: That amenity area is on a point in the lake, with two pools joined by a waterfall and a clubhouse with a gym.
use: That amenity area is on a point in the lake, with two pools joined by waterfalls and a clubhouse with a gym.

struck: Tennis and basketball courts and horseshoe pits are across the road.
use: Tennis and basketball courts are across the road, and the community has horseshoe pits.

struck: A court found no rule on the land that kept it a golf course, and the state Court of Appeals agreed in 2012.
use: The court sent the case to a special referee, who found no rule on that land that kept it a golf course. The state Court of Appeals upheld that finding in 2012.

pattern: \bFew homes in the two sections come up for sale
struck: Few homes in the two sections come up for sale.
use: (Cut it: 17 resales in about 250 homes in a year, and no row compares turnover with other places.)

pattern: \bfew homes are sold by their owners
struck: Builders sold new townhomes here in the past year, but few homes are sold by their owners.
use: (Cut the clause after 'but': 10 resales in about 260 homes in a year, and no row compares turnover with other places.)

pattern: \babout 20 minutes, the longest of the four
struck: The drive to the beach takes about 20 minutes, the longest of the four Carolina Forest neighborhoods here.
use: The drive to the beach takes about 15 to 20 minutes, about the same as from Waterbridge.

struck: Pine Lakes Country Club opened in 1927 as Ocean Forest Country Club, Myrtle Beach's first golf course, and took the name Pine Lakes in 1946.
use: Pine Lakes Country Club opened in 1927 as Ocean Forest Country Club, Myrtle Beach's first golf course, and took the name Pine Lakes in the 1940s.

struck: Grand Park, with picnic shelters, ball fields and a playground, is a two-minute walk from the nearest homes.
use: Grand Park, with picnic shelters, ball fields and a playground, is a two-minute walk from the middle of the neighborhood.

pattern: \bgrew into an Air Force base after the war
struck: The base began as an Army Air Corps field in World War II, grew into an Air Force base after the war, and closed in 1993.
use: The base began as an Army Air Corps field in World War II, became an Air Force base in 1954, and closed in 1993.

pattern: \bRiver Oaks Elementary School and the Berkshire Village section are both on Augusta Plantation Drive
struck: River Oaks Elementary School and the Berkshire Village section are both on Augusta Plantation Drive.
use: River Oaks Elementary School, on Augusta Plantation Drive, is a 2-minute drive from the Berkshire Village section.

struck: The residential association started the same day, and neighborhoods grew up around the courses.
use: The residential association's covenants were recorded the same day, and neighborhoods grew up around the courses.
